title: storage_pointer and registration are unauthenticated on the received-block path (outside both the block hash and the FALCON envelope)
failure: Any gossip relay (repropagate_block is live, block_handlers.rs:287-299) can rewrite a validly-signed block in transit: swap shard_hashes/placements so the victim's chain 'authorizes' attacker-chosen shard IDs anchored to a legitimate asset (and A6.6 registration_for_shard then serves the forged registration onward); swap registration.network_scope to pick which network's D4 rules validate the proof; swap registration.authorization.owners to make the attacker the asset's owner for seal/distribution-right decisions. Every check in insert_received_block still passes.

title: Network-scope shared chain cannot converge in production: adopt_genesis unwired and a foreign genesis is uninsertable
failure: Genesis is deterministic per (device, coordinate, epoch), so two distinct devices always have different geneses. A joiner records the network's root, then every fetched network block is orphaned (unknown predecessor) or hard-rejected, and the orphans can never link because their root genesis can never be inserted. CLAUDE.md's 'Network sync MVP working / cross-genesis insertion' is not achievable on the shipped accept path — sync converges only between nodes sharing a genesis, which production never creates. The S3.4 container that was supposed to hold device + adopted network chains side by side (chain.rs:700-703) shipped as ReceivedAssetStore, which holds asset chains, not network block chains.

title: Catch-up sync stalls: TransportSyncDriver flips SyncManager to Synchronized after every successful round regardless of remaining lag
failure: A node 500 blocks behind fetches 50, is marked Synchronized at the peer's height, and the 5s loop never pulls that network again. Re-entry requires a live Announce exceeding last_height + max_block_lag (100) — on a quiescent chain the node stays permanently 450 blocks behind; on a growing chain it catches up at most 50 blocks per 100-block-lag trigger, i.e. diverges. The driver conflates 'round succeeded' with 'chain synchronized'.

title: Received blocks bypass ChainValidator entirely, and the max_block_size cap is decorative because Block::size() is a fixed-formula estimate
failure: A peer ships a block whose one entry carries a 200 MB Local{path} payload: it measures ~520 'bytes', passes every accept check, is fsync'd through the BlockSink, counted wrong in stats.total_data_size, and repropagated to other peers. The only actual bound is whatever the STOQ stream read imposes, which is a transport accident, not a chain rule.

title: proof_hash and the FALCON envelope are defined over non-canonical serde_json — every StateProof schema change invalidates all previously signed blocks cross-version
failure: A verifier running code with one more StateProof field re-serializes an old proof WITH the new null/zero keys, producing different bytes than the producer hashed and signed → 'proof_hash mismatch (integrity violation)' and envelope rejection for every pre-upgrade block. Today this is masked by the wipe-all-data-on-format-change policy, which cannot survive a real multi-version network (roadmap J rolling upgrades) — the S3.2/S3.3 field additions already crossed this line once.

title: #52 confirmed: parse_and_verify_block is a duplicate received-block validation site using intrinsic validate() outside the D4 scope seam
failure: Two transcriptions of the received-entry rule that can drift: once a network publishes a ruleset more permissive than intrinsic validate(), the announce pre-filter silently drops (returns None, no insert error) blocks the D4 resolver would accept — and the drop happens before the S3.2-F2 REJECTED warn, so it is also less observable. Today it is pure redundant work per announced block.

title: BlockPropagator.seen_blocks grows without bound on the live propagation path
failure: One map entry per block hash ever propagated, each holding a coordinate set, retained for process lifetime — a slow, monotonic leak on a long-running reflector, violating the substrate rule that network-fed maps must be bounded (the same class P6 fixed for the orphan buffer and S3.4 fixed for the pools).

title: Received-entry mirror_seal authority is unchecked — a peer can deliver on-chain seals attributed to identities that never authorized them
failure: A peer sends a block whose MirrorSeal.sealed_by is neither the FALCON-bound author nor an owner in the asset's AuthorizationSet; it becomes hash-committed mirror history under a forged sealer identity. (Partially subsumed by the registration-unauthenticated finding — authorization itself is forgeable in transit — but the gate is missing even for honest registrations.)

title: Dead genesis-auth MFA subsystem (~770 lines) protecting a placeholder random-bytes 'keypair'
failure: Reads as a shipped security feature (MFA-protected genesis credentials) but is unreachable, and if ever wired as-is it would MFA-protect cryptographically meaningless bytes — a claimed-security lie waiting to be believed.

title: genesis_assessor.rs is a dead parallel hardware-assessment/genesis-asset path (also the only producer of the decorative AssetAddress records)
failure: Two implementations own 'assess hardware for genesis' with different outputs (GenesisAssetRecord+AssetAddress vs HardwareAssessment→StateProof); readers and future R1 work can wire the dead one; it also keeps the decorative AssetAddress pipeline looking consumed when it is not.

title: errors.rs structured error types are dead — the entire blockchain API returns Result<T, String>
failure: The re-export advertises an error architecture that nothing implements; String errors make the accept-path rejections unmatchable by callers (block_handlers can only log, never branch on rejection kind).

title: Two block-persistence stacks: live BlockSink/PersistenceManager vs ChainStateManager (state.rs) off the daemon path
failure: Two on-disk block formats/directory layouts that cannot see each other: blocks written by MatrixFoundation-based storage flows are invisible to a restart's from_blocks (which reads the PersistenceManager store), and doc-readers wire the wrong one (mod.rs presents create_node_blockchain as THE constructor).

title: D4 fail-closed hook (resolve_strict) built but inactive, and NetworkRuleSet::publish has zero production callers
failure: The canonical 'validation = the rules of the NETWORK for a given asset' is structurally routed (both local and received paths share the seam — good) but semantically inert: an unadopted/hostile network's assets validate against the default anchor forever, and nothing fails closed. Status claims of 'per-network validation (D4) complete' overstate what runs.

title: H3 unsigned-envelope debt in e2e tests: network_sync_e2e and scaling_integration build unsigned entries and expect insert_received_block to accept them
failure: These integration tests fail by default and only pass with the migration flag exported externally — the flag intended as a one-release migration is now load-bearing test infrastructure, which is exactly how it survives into production deployment scripts.

title: Sync push/pull ownership split across two parallel message vocabularies with manual conversion
failure: Adding or changing a sync message requires touching two enums plus two converters, and the pairs can silently diverge (Genesis/Header/Block variants already dispatch at different layers per sync_manager.rs:441-452); the dead trailing field wastes 40 bytes per announce and misleads readers into thinking a second integrity check exists.

title: 'spine' vocabulary survives as serialized wire field names (spine_point/spine_seq) and as the primary doc vocabulary of the chain core
failure: The canonical model bans the privileged-spine framing; a serialized field name is load-bearing (renaming changes the attestation wire/signing preimage since proof_bytes cover canonical fields), so the scar tissue is now baked into signatures — the longer it ships, the more expensive the rename.

title: Device-scope announce dedup keys on block INDEX across independent chains
failure: A spine-offset assumption surviving in exactly the scope where it is meaningless: a foreign device block at index <= our height is silently skipped as 'already have', while one above our height proceeds to insert_received_block only to be rejected/orphaned on linkage anyway — the gate does no valid work and reads as cross-chain index comparability, the exact confusion the unification removed elsewhere.

title: 500-line bar: chain.rs (1469) and mutations.rs (1479) confirmed over, with real mixed-concern seams
failure: Not style: the accept gate and the lineage rules are the two most security-sensitive functions in the crate and currently share a file with the convenience producers (register_dns_asset etc.), which is how a duplicate site like #52 goes unnoticed — the single-gate property is invisible at file granularity.

title: D3/S3.4 accept-lineage subsystem is receive-only: zero production producers for asset-chain presentation, mirror attestation, and sealing
failure: Two live HyperMesh nodes will never exchange an asset chain or a mirror attestation: nothing ever opens the sending stream, so accept_asset_chain and accept_wire_attestation are dead-on-arrival in the shipped binary despite task #48 ('D3 — Wire the accept path to the network (production caller)') being marked completed. The S3.5 car-title transfer story (hand the recipient the verified history) and the S3.3 mirror-evidence story (mirror attests after validating a fetch) have no producing call site — the feature is presented as wired but is dormant end-to-end.

title: Received-block mirror_seal accepted without any seal-authority check; local seal path rejects every real asset (ownerless), so on-chain seal attribution is unenforced
failure: A peer can insert on-chain, hash-committed 'mirror history' attributed to an identity that never authorized it (seal forgery survives the H3 signer binding because sealed_by is not checked against stake_holder_id or the AuthorizationSet). Meanwhile the honest local seal path can never run for a real daemon-created asset, so S3.3's 'sealed into the spine by the owner' (commit eb073315) is unreachable in practice: the only seals that can exist on a live mesh are received, unauthorized ones.

title: #52 confirmed open: block_handlers.rs pre-validation is a second transcription of the received-block gate, using the intrinsic validate() instead of the D4 resolver
failure: Two lists of the same rule — exactly the drift class the codebase's own S3.3 docs condemn ('one gate, not two', asset_chain_handlers.rs:7-17). The day a NetworkRuleSet publishes a bar different from the intrinsic StateProof::validate() (the whole point of D4/resolve_strict), announced blocks get dropped or passed by the announce pre-filter at :115 before the resolver ever sees them, and the announce path silently diverges from the sync-fetch path. Today it is also duplicate CPU (every announced block's proofs serialized+hashed twice).

title: Stale deferral in accept_wire_attestation: 'no wire caller can reach the received side of holds_asset' is no longer true since D3 landed
failure: An authenticated peer can adopt up to 1024 received chains (its own cheap self-signed assets), then flood attestations about those received-only assets into the SHARED 32 MiB MirrorAttestationPool. Reject-not-evict means nothing recorded is deleted, but the pool fills with statements about assets this container merely caches, and honest attestations for assets the container actually owns are refused (delay primitive) — the exact coupling the comment itself names as 'the gate S3.5 will need'.

title: Documented operator reclaim valves (forget/clear) are unreachable in the shipped binary; received store and attestation pool are memory-only
failure: The reject-not-evict design is sound only with a working release valve; without one, a store/pool at capacity refuses every newcomer until process restart — and restart wipes ALL adopted 'verified history that a caller may already have acted on' (store.rs:157-158) plus every pooled attestation, because nothing is durable. The docs' load-bearing operator story is fiction in the shipped binary.

title: 'Spine' vocabulary survives the de-spine refactor as live type/field names, including a serialized wire field
failure: Load-bearing naming lie against the canonical model (no privileged linear spine; an attestation names a lineage_id — lib's own doc at attestation.rs:105 admits 'A spine_point is a lineage_id'). Every new reader re-imports the single-spine mental model from the type that is supposed to embody its replacement, and the refactor-complete claim is falsified by the surviving field.

title: F3 'capacity before FALCON' guarantee has a hole for extensions: early probe skipped when the chain is already held, but adopt can still refuse on bytes
failure: At byte-capacity, an authenticated peer that holds one adopted chain can repeatedly present extensions of it; each attempt costs full re-verification of up to MAX_RECEIVED_CHAIN_ENTRIES (512) FALCON-1024 signatures and is then refused at adopt-time — exactly the steady-state CPU-exhaustion shape the F3 early probe was built to close for new chains (store.rs:251-266's O(1)-refusal claim does not hold for this case).

title: Status verification: resolve_strict still inactive (as documented); insert_received_block no longer skips proof validation; H3 unsigned-block env flag still load-bearing in two test files
failure: The fail-closed per-network seam remains a no-op: an asset scoped to an unseen network silently resolves to anchor requirements (resolve, network_rules.rs:97) instead of being refused, so 'the rules of the NETWORK' is aspirational until activation. The env flag remaining in tests means signing in library-mode chains is still not universal, keeping a production escape hatch alive.

title: Reflector sync-pull is inert: gated SYNC/BLOCK_FETCH sent over the never-authenticated CONN_TYPE_PEER_MESSAGE connection are always dropped by the receiver auth gate
failure: A node polling a reflector via TransportSyncDriver::run_sync_round opens a fresh unauthenticated connection; the reflector silently drops its SyncRequest and BlockFetchRequest, so run_sync_round always returns zero fetched blocks. Reflector-based catch-up sync cannot deliver against any peer that enforces the gate. Only push block-propagation and heartbeats — which ride the existing handshake connection's run_peer_message_loop (background.rs:211 uses node.connection) — actually function, masking the dead pull path.

title: Mirror-attestation and presented-asset-chain SEND paths have no production caller — the wire surface is receive-only
failure: A node accepts and records attestations/asset-chains a peer sends, but never emits its own: after validating a fetched mirror it never signs and sends the 'I hold and validated asset A' attestation the owner needs, and a holder never presents an asset's sub-chain for adoption. The canonical mirror/attestation model's producing half is dormant; the seal-on-chain and adopt-off-spine machinery on the receiving side has no live source to consume in a real deployment.

title: #52 still open: block_handlers.parse_and_verify_block is a third per-entry validation site that bypasses the D4 ValidationService.validate_received seam
failure: When network-genesis rulesets are published and resolve_strict is activated at the single ValidationService seam, the block_handlers pre-check will still admit entries against the raw structural bar, silently diverging from the received-path policy — exactly the drift D4 was structured to prevent. Today it is redundant duplicate work on every received block.

title: Two overlapping gossip subsystems: TAG_GOSSIP (0x20) is sent live but its handler only logs and discards; real gossip rides CONN_TYPE_GOSSIP
failure: In Public mode both loops run: one GossipProtocol's state is merged and used, the other's TAG_GOSSIP broadcasts are pure wasted bandwidth whose received copies are logged and dropped. Two GossipProtocol instances hold divergent membership state; a reader of the Handler::Gossip arm would wrongly believe TAG_GOSSIP is a functional receive path.

title: Ungated state-mutating tags are reachable with no handshake via CONN_TYPE_PEER_MESSAGE, into unbounded stores
failure: An anonymous QUIC client (TLS is encryption-only under AcceptAllVerifier) can open a CONN_TYPE_PEER_MESSAGE connection and inject arbitrary share invites, direct messages, and key-rotation entries with no PoS handshake, growing inbox/message_store/rotation_chains without bound — a memory-DoS and store-pollution vector. Signature verification for invites/messages is deferred to a later accept flow, so storage happens first.

title: SwarmDemandTracker demand map and per-shard requester_ids grow without bound
failure: A long-running node that serves many distinct shards to many distinct peers accumulates one permanent (network,shard) entry per shard and one permanent node_id string per requester, forever. Memory grows monotonically with lifetime shard/peer diversity; the intelligence signal is also skewed by fetches that were subsequently refused by F6.

title: Dead/orphan tag space: CRL tags never routed, distributed-CA + legacy-transfer + key-rotation tags handled but never sent
failure: The tag table advertises a distributed-CA/CRL/transfer/key-rotation protocol that is inert: readers and the route unit-test table treat these as live wiring, but no peer ever emits them, and the CRL constants are unreachable. TAG_TRANSFER (0x07) also duplicates the intent of the 0x40-0x44 transfer tags with an insecure auto-accept stub.

title: peer_connection.rs (899 lines) and sync_and_reflection.rs (801 lines) violate the module's own <500-line contract; sync_and_reflection is an unrelated-handler grab-bag
failure: The stated per-file bound is silently broken; the grab-bag file forces unrelated handlers to share a change surface, raising merge/regression risk and making ownership of each concern unclear.

title: Replication-poll actuation discards replica bytes and registers phantom providership
failure: The loop 'converges' on phantom replicas: this node is handed out (via its own index, TAG_SHARD_LOCATE answers, and analytics replica counts) as a provider of a shard it never stored; peers directing fetches at it get empty responses. Replica accounting rises without any new copy existing anywhere — the popularity→replication loop is still open (2026-07-05 audit) but now actively corrupts provider data. A provider returning garbage is also 'fetched' successfully (no hash gate).

title: H3 feed loop re-feeds the full cumulative demand snapshot every 10s, and the trigger reads cumulative counts — signal inflates forever
failure: One real fetch of one shard produces +1 request_count and +1 consumer_position every 10s forever (~8.6k/day per requester per shard). `needed = ceil(request_count/100)` grows without bound, so every shard ever requested once eventually signals urgent replication permanently — perpetual 30s fetch churn (compounded by the discard bug) and a demand map whose k-means clusters are dominated by replayed history, not current demand.

title: Demand/analytics state is unbounded and remotely drivable
failure: An authenticated peer looping TAG_SHARD_FETCH with random 32-byte ids grows two maps plus a Vec per entry without bound on the serving node (amplified 1-per-10s by the feed loop) — memory exhaustion on long-lived nodes; violates the substrate-memory rule that RAM working sets evict, never grow unbounded.

title: DispersionAdvisor anti-affinity is a live no-op (fresh advisor each call, register_replica never fed)
failure: Replica-source recommendations never avoid positions already holding replicas, so fetches cluster onto already-served demand centroids instead of spreading — the documented dispersion behavior silently doesn't exist (confirms the suspected issue; cite-verified).

title: distribute_to_peers ignores the placement authority's chosen node and re-picks by announced coordinate
failure: When a peer's proximity cell differs from its announced cell (the normal case once RTT is measured), the shard is sent to a different peer than the one the PoS-eligibility+octant authority selected — and than the placement recorded on-chain by register_sharded_asset_onchain (ipc/handlers/store.rs:141-146), so the chain's placements point at cells whose nearest announced peer never received the shard.

title: Store/distribute path never populates ShardLocationIndex on any node
failure: Immediately after publish+distribute, no node's index knows any provider: directed fetch ordering degrades to blind peer scans, TAG_SHARD_LOCATE answers only cover self-held shards (sync_and_reflection.rs:152 compensates for self only), and the E.2 poll loop logs 'no remote providers ... yet' for exactly the shards that were just placed.

title: R4 Anonymous HashOnly dedup policy built and tested but never selected live
failure: A node running PrivacyMode::ANONYMOUS that fetches a shard registers itself as a provider and broadcasts TAG_SHARD_ANNOUNCE — exactly the identity/location disclosure R4's HashOnly policy exists to prevent; the R4 'privacy-scoped dedup' feature claim is only half-true live.

title: SpatialBucketAssigner (hash_bucket.rs) is dead in production — spatial block filtering never runs
failure: The 'Public mode block sync' spatial hash-bucket responsibility the module header claims is a fiction at runtime — Public nodes propagate NearestN(6) and accept without spatial bucketing; anyone reading the code or status assuming R12-style spatial responsibility is misled.

title: DefaultIsolationManager/MultiNetworkRegistry unmounted; NetworkId dimension is constant DEFAULT_NETWORK everywhere
failure: Shards do not actually belong to their network (canonical torrent/mirror model): a Private-mode node's announcements land in the same flat DEFAULT_NETWORK namespace as Public peers', and no isolation check exists on the replication/fetch path to stop cross-network provider leakage once multiple networks are real. The completed-task status overstates reality.

title: locality_centroids + GeographicClustering 'promotion to live' is false — zero callers
failure: Doc asserts a live capability (locality centroids driving demand placement) that does not execute; next reader builds on centroids that are never computed. provider_from_nodes in the same file IS live — the dead half hides behind the live half's credibility.

title: ngauge CollectiveIntelligence orphaned (re-export only, no consumers)
failure: 350+ lines of aggregation logic present as a live subsystem in the crate API; per the vector-space-regions memory it is the intended substrate for emergent-region work, so silent rot here is a future correctness trap.

title: handle_incoming_shard_stream is a prod-dead duplicate of handle_shard_message with divergent serve format
failure: Two owners of the shard wire protocol: a future edit to one (e.g., the envelope, or a size guard) silently misses the other, and the E2E test exercises the variant production never runs — green tests over dead code.

title: H4 propagation-weight computation runs on a fresh empty RoutingIntelligence every cycle (neutral by construction)
failure: A loop that logs 'Updated propagation weights from ngauge' machinery presents routing intelligence as live while the only real effect is the eBPF publish hook; MEMORY's 'PropagationWeight 15s' status overstates this.

title: Live demand feed re-ingests cumulative snapshot every 10s: unbounded consumer_positions + popularity inflates with uptime
failure: With ZERO new traffic, one past requester of one shard adds one MatrixPosition and +1 request_count every 10s forever: (a) memory leaks at ~(shards x requesters) positions per 10s and cluster_positions' k-means (swarm_analytics.rs:630-680) iterates the whole vector per poll, so CPU grows linearly with uptime; (b) request_count measures uptime, not demand — ReplicationTrigger's needed=ceil(count/100) (swarm_analytics.rs:488-492) ratchets to max_replicas=20 for any shard fetched once, so the P6 'converged' loop perpetually re-fires and over-replicates everything.

title: DispersionAdvisor anti-affinity is a live no-op (constructed fresh each cycle; register_replica never called)
failure: New replicas are steered purely by demand k-means and can land exactly on nodes already holding the shard; the documented/status-claimed anti-affinity dispersion property does not exist at runtime, silently degrading R12 dispersion.

title: H4 propagation-weight loop computes weights from a fresh, never-fed RoutingIntelligence — permanently neutral, presented as live intelligence
failure: set_propagation_weights receives all-1.0 factors every cycle; the claimed intelligence-driven block propagation weighting (crate-status 'Routing intelligence feedback consumed by blockmatrix', MEMORY 'PropagationWeight 15s') is decorative, and the info log actively misreports it as working. Also doubly broken because the pipeline that would feed it receives no frames (see MetricsReporter finding).

title: CLI `hypermesh ngauge marketplace|metrics|leases` call IPC methods the daemon never registers
failure: Three advertised CLI subcommands always fail at runtime with a method-not-found service_error against a healthy daemon — user-visible dead surface presenting as features.

title: blockmatrix still declares reed-solomon-erasure dependency it no longer uses (A1 leftovers)
failure: Dead dependency implies a second RS engine still exists in blockmatrix, confusing future audits and inflating the dependency tree/build of the deploy binary.

title: spine_point/spine_seq are wire-visible serde field names in the public signed MirrorAttestation type
failure: The one type third parties sign and every peer parses teaches the dead single-spine model; every new consumer of the attestation wire re-learns 'spine' as if it were authoritative, when the value is actually a lineage_id. The scar is now frozen into cross-version JSON wire compat, getting more expensive to remove with every deploy.

title: "spine/off-spine" vocabulary saturates the accept/attestation/lineage path docs despite the spine being declared non-authoritative
failure: Docs present the deprecated container-chain as the system's backbone. A reader of the accept path concludes the linear chain is the authority and per-asset lineage is the satellite — the exact inversion of the D1 model — and designs new features against the wrong frame.

title: Reputation-as-float serde fields with live defaults in the mounted user-contribution platform config
failure: Directly violates the no-reputation-floats canon (PoS is binary authentic-or-not) in serde-visible config that ships in the mounted platform. Decorative today (nothing reads the values), so it is dead economics presenting as a live reputation system — the next contributor will 'finish' it by wiring reputation math.

title: crate-status.toml claims a working "Genesis adoption protocol" while adopt_genesis is documented NOT WIRED
failure: The status feed (generated scripts/output/status.ts:173 repeats it) advertises a joining mechanism that the code itself says must not be wired; anyone triaging network-join work trusts the status file and skips the real gap. Also perpetuates "foreign genesis" scar vocabulary in the shipped feature description.

title: audit_ledger doc cross-references the dissolved "foreign store"; other doc/log "foreign" survivals
failure: audit_ledger points maintainers at a module that no longer exists; the doc/log uses of "foreign" keep the deleted foreign-chain concept alive in grep results and operator logs, blurring the line between the dead second-class-chain model and plain English "another network's".

title: catalog module file security/reputation.rs survives the ReputationSystem->PublisherAuthenticator rename
failure: The import path catalog::security::reputation::PublisherAuthenticator re-introduces the banned concept at every use site; the module name contradicts its own contents and the terminology canon (BinaryAuthenticator model).

title: Prod code hardcodes NetworkId([0u8;16]) instead of DEFAULT_NETWORK
failure: The default-network fact is owned in two-plus places; if DEFAULT_NETWORK is ever changed or replaced by real network routing, these sites silently keep keying the zero network and the eBPF privacy-action / engagement-metrics paths diverge from the analytics keyed on the constant.

title: stoq reuses the DEFAULT_NETWORK byte value as an "unknown network" sentinel in rejection reasons
failure: A rejection that means "I don't know which path/network you came from" is indistinguishable from "tunnel from the default network to X is not configured". Any diagnostic or policy consumer keying on `from == DEFAULT_NETWORK` misreads unknown-path errors as default-network tunnel misconfiguration.

title: Stale comments claim trust-score/reputation logic where the code is canon-compliant
failure: Comments assert the banned trust-score/reputation model over code that correctly implements binary authentication and capacity selection — a reviewer greps 'trust score', concludes a scoring system exists (or should), and either files false canon violations or builds one to match the comment.

title: Stake-as-magnitude vocabulary: dead StakeAmount criterion variant and Caesar mock staking-APY API
failure: StakeAmount is a validation criterion that, if ever wired, would gate transitions on a stake magnitude — the exact rejected model; today it is dead weight contradicting the adjacent canon comments. Caesar's UI handler serves fabricated coin-staking economics (APY, lock periods) that conflate PoStake-as-authorization with coin staking and present as a real feature to any UI consumer.

title: DefaultIsolationManager confirmed unmounted — deliberately re-orphaned by de-worlds; no per-network fetch isolation exists live
failure: The canonical claim 'shards belong to their NETWORK, complete isolation' has no live enforcement beyond a single-network handshake string compare; a node participating in two networks (the target model) has zero mechanism preventing cross-network shard/metadata flow. Task #59 'P5 Mount IsolationManager' reads completed but the mount was reverted — status is a lie relative to the tracker.

title: TAG_SHARD_ANNOUNCE and TAG_SHARD_LOCATE bypass the auth gate: unauthenticated index poisoning, provider-topology leakage, unbounded index growth
failure: An unauthenticated peer can (a) poison the location index so the E.2 replication loop (replication_service/poll.rs:97-137) fetches replicas from an attacker node, (b) enumerate which nodes — including this one — hold any content hash, leaking provider topology and 'I hold shard X' identity in Private networks (exactly ViolationType::IdentityLeakage the dormant isolation module was built to prevent), and (c) grow the index without bound by spamming unique hashes faster than the 30s cleanup_expired cadence reclaims them.

title: Live shard demand/location/replication all keyed to DEFAULT_NETWORK — the peer's authenticated network never reaches the (NetworkId, ContentHash) indexes
failure: Per-network fetch isolation is structurally present but behaviorally absent: two networks served by one node pool their providers, demand, and replication targets in one bucket, so a shard private to network A can be selected as a replication source/target in the context of network B. The Track-P keying is currently decorative — the exact 'built-but-not-wired' pattern.

title: Network identity has three live representations that never convert: String (auth/sync/dns), lib NetworkId (placement), NetworkScope (validation); nesting APIs are type-incompatible and unwired
failure: The same fact ('which network') is owned by four types with no bridge: a membership's parent can never be populated from the only live producer of parents (DNS), and any future code comparing a membership's String id to a placement NetworkId or a validation NetworkScope must invent an ad-hoc conversion, guaranteeing drift. Nested-network resolution ('walk the parent chain', sync_manager.rs:119-121 doc) cannot work because parents are never recorded.

title: Dormant triple-stack multi-network subsystem (trust/ + multi_network.rs + assets/multi_node coordinator): placeholder crypto, fake cross-network validation, doc claims it is live
failure: Three parallel dormant implementations of 'join/leave networks with isolation' present as working multi-network participation (crate-status/docs), and the fake structural cross-network validation could be mistaken for the real dual-proof transfer path (the live TAG_TRANSFER_* handlers) and wired somewhere by a future contributor. StoqIsolationManager (multi_network_coordinator.rs:51-128) is additionally a naming lie — a blockmatrix HashMap that never touches stoq.

title: Four isolation-manager implementations across three modules/crates, zero mounted — one fact ('may traffic cross networks') with no owner
failure: Cross-network boundary enforcement has four competing definitions and no live one; any attempt to 'turn on isolation' must first litigate which of the four is real, and stoq carrying a full isolation subsystem violates 'stoq = transport only' separation.

title: Retired 4-tier taxonomy survives as two NetworkType enums plus four Tier structs, contradicting the canonical 2-axis PrivacyMode
failure: Three surfaces claim to be 'the network type'; a contributor choosing which enum to consume (e.g. when mounting isolation) gets steered into the retired taxonomy, and the false '1:1' doc invites conflating CA-endpoint choice with PrivacyMode.

title: Top-level privacy/ module (2832 lines: tiers, switching, policies, ebpf bridge) has zero production consumers but is documented as the live tier-enforcement layer
failure: Tier/policy enforcement appears implemented (and is test-covered!) while the live node enforces nothing from this module — a reader auditing 'is Private mode enforced?' finds 2832 lines of green-tested machinery that never runs; the ebpf_integration bridge additionally overlaps the real hypermesh-ebpf policy path.

title: NetworkMembership.privacy_mode is decorative on the sync path; reflector heartbeats hardcode PrivacyMode::PUBLIC
failure: A Private or Anonymous network's reflector pool records all members as PUBLIC; any privacy-aware reflector selection, reward computation, or disclosure decision built on the pool will treat bounded-network members as fully public — silent privacy-classification corruption in live state.
